claims.text: Multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloys can form a dense protective oxide film at elevated temperature.
The relevant high-temperature protective oxide is a spinel-type layer.
Mechanical sliding or impact repeatedly disrupts the protective oxide film.
Disruption of the oxide film exposes fresh reactive metal surfaces.
Freshly exposed metal surfaces corrode more rapidly than oxide-covered surfaces.
Corrosion compromises or weakens the alloy's local microstructure.
Corrosion-induced microstructural weakening increases susceptibility to further wear.
Wear-assisted corrosion and corrosion-assisted wear form a self-reinforcing positive-feedback loop.
Surface enrichment in elements such as Al and Fe predisposes the eutectic alloy to form a dense protective oxide.
Temperatures of approximately 800–900 °C in a NaCl-containing environment enable in situ formation of the proposed oxide film.
An intact oxide film shields the alloy from corrosion.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion produces a significantly higher total degradation rate than isolated wear or isolated corrosion.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion increases wear depth relative to isolated-condition baselines.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion increases corrosion rate relative to isolated-condition baselines.
A temperature above 800 °C is required for sufficient protective-film formation in the proposed system.
Artificial stabilization of the oxide film should suppress the coupled-degradation acceleration.
Under isolated wear or corrosion, the protective oxide has an uninterrupted opportunity to form and stabilize.
The magnitude of synergistic acceleration depends on oxide stability, microstructural heterogeneity, and the intensity or frequency of wear cycles.

contradictions.description: The corrosive environment is alternately described as a chloride-containing solution, a NaCl-containing atmosphere, and a corrosive medium at 800–900 °C. These are materially different test environments, and an ordinary aqueous solution is incompatible with that temperature range unless exceptional pressure conditions are specified.

The prediction only states that coupled degradation exceeds either isolated baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires it to exceed the sum of isolated wear and corrosion rates. The latter is a substantially stronger synergy criterion than the stated prediction.
